reports.source_note: HAI 21.03 — HIL-based Augmented ICS Security Dataset [test] — prepared from hai-21.03-test1.csv.gz, downsampled to every 10th row, dropped attack_P1, attack_P2, attack_P3 | test slice of a three-way split, train_fraction=0.04 calib_fraction=0.3 | Coarse-map inflation: HAI's declared topology could not be partitioned below process level for P1 and P2, so unrelated departures anywhere on one process collapse into a single subsystem event. A large reduction here is evidence that grouping is correctly IMPLEMENTED, not that it is correctly RESOLVED. A finer map would lower the headline number and raise its meaning. | Uncalibrated hypothesis confidence: the confidences on these hypotheses are NOT calibrated probabilities and must not be surfaced to a user under Constitution §3.3. Three reasons, and the third is measured rather than asserted. (1) The template priors are reasoned placeholders, not measured base rates. (2) EVIDENCE_STRENGTH is a placeholder too, and measuring either needs data labelling WHICH EXPLANATION IS TRUE, which no corpus PHOS uses carries — HAI labels attack and normal. (3) The belief update treats each subsystem event as independent, and on a plant they are plainly not: one disturbance persisting across consecutive windows arrives as many near-identical events, so a confidence built from them counts one cause many times. Atlas may rank and reason over these hypotheses; it may not present their confidences as calibrated. Evidence weights, separately, are calibrated. | Co-occurring-fault masking: a coarse group can hide a second, unrelated event inside one subsystem event. Two independent faults on one process are indistinguishable from one, and an attack co-occurring with a fault is reported as a single thing to investigate. That is a recall risk carried by the grouping, not a win. | Grouped weight is a maximum: a subsystem event carries the strongest member's calibrated weight, and a maximum over a set of calibrated probabilities is not itself a calibrated probability — it is biased upward by how many signals the unit carries. The calibration error reported for subsystem events may therefore come out better or worse than the per-signal one for reasons that have nothing to do with the calibrator, and is not a reading of it. | Saturated false-positive load: when a declared SaturationPolicy fires, the row is REFUSED as a detection claim even if recall looks excellent. Metrics stay on the report; they must not be quoted as detection. Public distillation 18.72 and Data4Cyber Track A keep their log names and stay MEASURED unless a caller applies a policy. Do not raise dwell_samples to chase a quieter public ZIP. | Normal-score CDF weights are not attack probabilities: the map is the empirical CDF of held-out attack-free magnitudes (ADR 0083). A weight of 0.9 means the score sits at or above about 90% of ordinary scores the model saw on normal data — not that an attack is 90% likely. Do not quote ECE against attack labels as evidence that these weights are calibrated probabilities under Constitution §3.3.
